I've been on this land for 40 years, since I was 34. Never went to school, not one day, but the land taught me everything I need. My son works in a shoe factory in Shijiazhuang and sends money home when he can. My daughter-in-law has a job at the township market. My grandson is in middle school. Most days it's just me walking these 5 mu, but my son comes back for the busy seasons — planting and harvest — and my daughter-in-law helps on weekends.

My wheat went in last October around the 12th, same date I always pick. I used our own saved seed, good heavy kernels from autumn 2023, soaked them in that red seed medicine before sowing. Before planting I broadcast about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — the kind with three numbers on the bag. Then in late March when the wheat greened up, I walked through with a basket and scattered about 40 jin of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang's wife tried using less fertilizer last year and her wheat came up thin as grass — she's regretting it now. I'm 74. I can't gamble on a bad year. Better to put a little too much than too little.

Now it's April, the wheat looks alright, about knee-high. I'll irrigate once more before the ears come out, maybe twice if the sky stays dry. Pumping water costs electricity money, but without it the grain won't fill properly. I already sprayed herbicide once in early spring. If I see aphids on the back of the leaves or if yellow rust shows up, I'll spray again. I expect about 800 jin per mu — same as most years, unless something goes wrong.

For the maize, after the combine cuts the wheat in early June, we don't rest. The window is tight — if you wait three days you're already late. My son tills quick with the tractor, then we plant with the hand planter. I buy hybrid seed from Old Chen's shop in the village, 3 jin per mu, costs about 50 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 60 jin per mu. When the stalks get to knee height — around mid-July — I topdress with about 40 jin of urea per mu. I water once or twice in summer, depending on whether the rains come. Spray herbicide when the weeds show up. Last year the maize gave me 900 jin per mu. I hope for the same this year.

I don't hire much labor — my family does most of it. Maybe 3–4 days of hired help for harvest if my son's factory won't give him leave. Total costs run about 2,700 yuan for both crops. The fertilizer is the biggest bite, then the maize seed, then electricity for pumping. It's a lot for us, but we need the grain for eating and for selling.
